Subject: RFP follow-up: price match details and migration support

Karthik,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency profile on the clinical workload. Procurement asked me to follow up with the concrete economics so they can compare apples-to-apples with the incumbent (ModelFlow).

Two asks:
- Can Redwood match or better the unit pricing ModelFlow provided (they quoted $0.020/token for generation and $0.003/embedding for the first 12 months)?
- What migration incentives do you offer for moving 3 production models (2 chat, 1 embedding) onto dedicated capacity? We have a hard requirement for an SLA and isolated data plane.

If you can send a simple table (tokens, embeddings, storage, monthly committed throughput) and a recommended migration credit structure, procurement can prioritize the vendor swap.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara — appreciate the clarity. Attaching a compact price matrix and a migration credit plan for the three-model transition (see attachments). High level summary below:

Offer snapshot (first 12 months):
- Generation: $0.019/token (12mo match, includes 5% starter credit against first 3 months consumption)
- Embeddings: $0.0025/embedding (12mo match)
- Dedicated pool reservation: 2 x A40-equivalent GPUs (SLA-backed) + onboarding seat + 30 hours of migration engineering support
- Migration credit: $120,000 one-time amortized credit (applied across first 6 months) — intended to cover third-party egress & engineering runbooks

We include: prefix/KV caching recommendations and a staged canary rollout plan to keep latency within your P50/P95 targets. Please review the attached price_matrix_v2.xlsx and migration_credit_plan.pdf; happy to incorporate procurement wording for the contract.

If that looks directionally right, I’ll loop in Marissa for the formal concession approval and Jonas for finance sign-off.

Looping you both in — VoltHealth wants a price/credit package to match ModelFlow. I sketched the numbers below and attached the two docs. Key asks from the customer: price parity for tokens/embeddings for 12 months, dedicated pool + SLA, and help covering migration costs (egress + eng hours).

Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the draft. A few quick thoughts:

1) Credit structure: prefer shorter, milestone-driven credits. Propose $70k credit (applied first 3 months) + an additional $50k contingent on hitting go-live and P95 latency target (proof-of-performance within 45 days). Avoid open-ended multi-month credits; they set precedent.
2) Price match: okay to match incumbent for generation for 12 months, but cap the matched consumption to the first $350k of spend to limit exposure. After that, standard list pricing applies.
3) Embeddings: agree to a slightly deeper cut ($0.0024/embed) but only if they commit to a 12-month reserved pool.
4) Add technical onboarding SLA: 2-week dedicated runbook and one on-site (or remote) workshop for the migration window.

Also recommend offering an optional one-time migration accelerator bundle (extra 40 eng hours for $40k) if they want a faster cutover.

Jonas — I'll need your sign-off on the approval matrix before we send anything formal. If approved, Karthik should present a single 'offer summary' page to VoltHealth rather than an open-ended spreadsheet.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

--
Redwood internal

Marissa / Karthik — quick finance note:

- I ran a conservative NPV with your proposed $70k + $50k contingent split and the capped matched spend up to $350k. With our renewal assumptions and cross-sell, the model is workable if we enforce the cap and the performance gating.
- Please see attached approval sheet (narrow_approval_matrix.xlsx) — it lists the concession band I can approve up to without exec escalation. Anything beyond the $120k total credit or an uncapped matched volume needs VP sign-off.
- Also flag: if we include a latency SLA, add a rollback clause that lets us transition routing back to a fallback model in two hours in case of sustained SLO violations. That reduces operational risk.

If you incorporate these constraints I can sign-off and Karthik can send the formal term sheet.

Jonas
Head of Revenue Finance | Redwood Inference
